position: Defend American Agriculture; A Proper Mission Statement
proposal: The Mandate recommends that a new Administration announce principles by executive order that put food productivity and affordability ahead of climate and equity goals, remove references to transforming the food system from USDA's website and materials, and review programs that push preferred farming practices onto farmers (citing climate-smart agriculture and the $300 million Organic Transition Initiative). It also offers a narrower model mission statement centered on agricultural information and research, food-related safety threats, removal of foreign trade barriers and unjustified domestic barriers, and sound science.

status_summary: No executive order announcing principles of the kind the Mandate describes was found. USDA acted instead through program decisions: on 2025-04-14 it cancelled the Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities and replaced it with Advancing Markets for Producers, requiring at least 65 percent of federal funds to reach producers, and on 2025-06-17 it announced termination of more than 145 diversity, equity and inclusion awards (up to $148.6 million). On web material the record is mixed: USDA removed climate-related pages after the inauguration but told a federal court on 2025-05-13 that it would restore them, and a USDA page endorsing the goals of the UN Food Systems Summit, linked to a 2021 food systems report, remained readable on 2026-10-12. USDA's About page states a vision of economic opportunity, rural prosperity and conservation with no equity or climate wording, but no formal mission statement revision was found. Executive Order 14414 (signed 2026-06-25) directs USDA to maximize funding for its Regenerative Pilot Program, a practice-promotion step that runs against the Mandate's call to review programs steering farmers toward preferred practices; progress is set at 30 to reflect that and the restored web content.

timeline.event: USDA announced cancellation of the Partnerships for Climate-Smart Commodities, which it said had high administrative fees and sent under half of federal funding to farmers, and its reform into Advancing Markets for Producers using existing funds; projects are reviewed against three Farmer First priorities, including at least 65 percent of federal funds reaching producers, and eligible expenses incurred before 2025-04-13 are honored.

In a joint letter to the US District Court for the Southern District of New York, in a suit by farm and environmental groups, USDA committed to restore climate-change-related web content removed after the inauguration, per the plaintiffs' counsel.
USDA announced termination of more than 145 awards focused on diversity, equity and inclusion, with maximum savings of $148.6 million.
USDA released the National Farm Security Action Plan with seven priority areas centered on farm and food security, including America First priorities across USDA programs.

Executive Order 14414 (signed 2026-06-25, published 2026-06-30 at 91 FR 39841) states a policy of advancing precision agriculture and regenerative research and practices, citing yields, input costs and profitability, and directs USDA to maximize funding for the existing Regenerative Pilot Program and evaluate expanding it; it directs EPA, HHS and USDA on chemical-exposure research, and does not mention climate, organic or equity or direct a review of USDA's mission.

title: Put food productivity ahead of climate and equity goals and narrow USDA's mission
uncertainties: No executive order setting agricultural principles was found in a Federal Register search of executive orders mentioning agriculture since 2025-01-20; EO 14414 was read in full on federalregister.gov (signed 2026-06-25, published 2026-06-30, 91 FR 39841) and concerns practices and chemical-exposure research, not principles, and does not mention climate, organic farming or equity. USDA's About page was re-read on 2026-10-17: it carries a vision statement on rural opportunity, agricultural output and conservation, with no equity or climate wording, but it mentions environmental markets including carbon, and no separately labeled mission statement; no new strategic plan was found. The USDA Office of the Chief Economist food systems page, which supports the UN Food Systems Summit goals, was still published on 2026-10-12; that read is not a dated government action and was removed from the timeline. The status of the Organic Transition Initiative after January 2025 was not found. The court outcome of the web-page lawsuit beyond the restoration commitment, which rests on a party press release, was not established. The cancellation of the climate-smart program is treated as aligned with the recommendation to review practice-pushing programs, which is an interpretation. The Mandate's model mission statement is addressed partly to Congress.
